analysis.title: "As Challenging As We Have Seen": Goldman's Panic Index Hits Record 9.8 After Fifth-Biggest VIX Spike On Record... Here's What Happened After The Other Four
key_insights: Goldman's derivatives desk calls the market 'as challenging as we have seen'. The S&P fell seven straight sessions, the VIX rose more than 16 points in a week (fifth-largest weekly spike on record), and the US Vol Panic Index hit a record 9.8 out of 10.

Weekly scoreboard: S&P closed at 6,910, down 8.6% on the week and up 0.9% YTD. Nasdaq 100 fell 10.4% (worst week since March 2020) and is more than 20% below its Oct 6 high. SOX fell 17%, its worst week since September 2011.
Cross-asset liquidation: gold fell 9.5%, bitcoin 14.2%, copper more than 9%. Only Treasuries worked, with the 10Y yield down 19bps to 4.94%.
Thematic baskets show a liquidation: Drones -24.8%, Bitcoin Sensitive -24.0%, Quantum Computing -23.4%, NeoClouds -22.6%, Space & Satellites -19.9%. The best basket, Bond Proxies, lost 1.9%.

Friday catalysts per the cash desk: Nvidia SEC probe headlines and an FT report that hawkish officials in Washington and Israel urge Trump to restart strikes on Iran, on top of a fragile tape after the biggest IPO ever failed to steady nerves.

After the four larger weekly VIX spikes (Oct 2008, May 2010, Feb 2020, Apr 2025), the S&P averaged +5.1% next day, +3.3% after one week (up every time), -2.8% after two weeks (lower 3 of 4), -0.7% after one month, and +26.5% after one year. Goldman says readings above 9.5 on the Panic Index have historically signaled near-term relief.

Goldman's technical view is a near-term bounce, but the market keeps struggling until there is clarity on the Fed path and the future of the AI trade. Drivers cited are FCI tightening, AI trade unwind, overseas tensions and a Fed tightening cycle.
Liquidity is thin: ETFs were above 39% of the tape on Friday and S&P top-of-book liquidity was $4MM, near the YTD low. Moves were larger than the flows.
Dealers are short gamma, after being the most short gamma since 2019 earlier in the week, which the desk expects to feed big moves.

CTAs are net short $19BN of US equities after selling $57BN in a month, and Goldman's model has them selling over the next week in every scenario. S&P trigger levels are 7,596, 7,540 and 7,119, all above the 6,910 close.

Funding cracked: the December S&P total return future slid from about FF+35 to about FF+20 into Friday's close after hedge funds covered about $25BN of futures shorts. Year-end funding is still at FF+100.
Nasdaq 100 is technically oversold with a 14-day RSI of 26.5, and the desk thinks systematic selling in Nasdaq futures is nearer its end than its start.

Copper fell more than 9% on tighter financial conditions and data center weakness, triggering CTA selling. Physical users were already loaded, with gross longs near 20% of open interest on Nov 10 (about double the norm), possibly front-running a US copper tariff, so they could not absorb the unwind.

TMT trader Peter Callahan: Nasdaq 100 had a bottom-five week of the past 20 years and US financial conditions are the tightest in over two years. Valuations are at 10-year lows (17x forward for Nasdaq 100, 12-13x for semis), but investors are on a buyers' strike with no identifiable catalyst despite beat-and-raise quarters from Keysight, Nvidia and Palo Alto.
Charts vs companies: names that have already cut (FFIV, INTC) are trading well relative, suggesting the market is front-running estimate cuts that companies and most investors do not expect.
Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all published 2027 S&P targets of 8,700, a 26% rally from Friday's close, which implies likely revisions.

Sector color: industrials and materials lost about 7%. Levered small and mid caps were hit (TROX -42%, YSS -35%, FLY -30%, FMC -22%). Data center names fell (MTZ -20%, VRT, FPS, INIO -18%). Housing was the rare winner on lower rates.
Health care had a policy scare from the CRUSH/RADV proposal, vertical break-up calls and Medicare-for-All headlines, hitting managed care, hospitals, medtech and biopharma.
Energy: Brent is down 15% in a month, refiners are the most shorted corner of the sector, and US natural gas is one of the better-owned hiding spots.

Outlook: the options market prices a 3.27% S&P move through Nov 27 with a Thursday holiday and Friday half day. The author says rent the one-week bounce but respect the two-week trapdoor, since all four prior panics ended with a policy rescue and the Fed is still hiking.

market_movers.rationale: Late-day headlines on an SEC probe hit the tape Friday, despite a beat-and-raise quarter last week.

sector_views.rationale: Oversold with 10-year-low valuations (17x Nasdaq 100, 12-13x semis), but a buyers' strike and possible estimate cuts leave no catalyst.
Each lost about 7% on the week, with levered small and mid caps hit by balance sheet and earnings worries.
Policy scare from CRUSH/RADV and Medicare-for-All headlines hit managed care and spread to hospitals, medtech and biopharma.
Conversations are more cautious into year-end with Brent down 15% in a month.
Rare winner on sharply lower rates.

earnings_insights: Last week brought beat-and-raise quarters from Keysight, Nvidia and Palo Alto, per Callahan, with firm compute pricing, but the market did not reward them.
Upcoming tech earnings Tuesday night: Dell, Workday, HP, plus Analog Devices, Autodesk, Nutanix, Zoom, HPE and Semtech.
Upcoming consumer earnings Tuesday: Best Buy, Dick's, Burlington, Dollar Tree, Abercrombie and Urban Outfitters. Deere earnings and guidance also due, along with PCE.
Names that already cut (F5, Intel) are outperforming, which suggests the market is pricing estimate cuts elsewhere.

trade_ideas.description: Rent the one-week bounce in S&P after the VIX spike, but respect the two-week downside
trade_ideas.rationale: The S&P was higher one week after all four larger VIX spikes, the Panic Index is near its ceiling and the Nasdaq is oversold.
trade_ideas.risk: CTA selling, short dealer gamma and a Fed that is still hiking could extend the drawdown.

risk_factors: CTA supply in every scenario and dealers short gamma.
Thin liquidity with a Thursday holiday and Friday half day.
Fed still hiking with no policy rescue visible.
AI trade unwind and possible estimate or capex cuts.
Funding premium could fade if the drawdown continues.
charts_described: Chart of every weekly VIX change since 1990 shows only four larger weeks: Oct 10, 2008, May 7, 2010, Feb 28, 2020 and April 4, 2025.
Table of S&P performance after the four prior VIX spikes: next day +5.1%, one week +3.3%, two weeks -2.8%, one month -0.7%, one year +26.5% on average.
Copper chart shows producers, merchants, processors and users' gross longs at about 20% of open interest on Nov 10, roughly double the norm.
vol_and_positioning: VIX closed above 37, up 92% on the week, and the term structure is steeply inverted with very steep skew.
Goldman US Vol Panic Index at a record 9.8 out of 10, with readings above 9.5 historically signaling near-term relief.
Dealers are short gamma, CTAs are net short $19BN with more selling expected, and S&P is below all CTA triggers (7,596, 7,540, 7,119).
Nasdaq 100 14-day RSI at 26.5. Systematic selling in Nasdaq futures is seen as closer to its end.
Non-systematic investors have not sold much, and the fast money has little net exposure left to sell per the author.
S&P options price a 3.27% move through Nov 27.
Funding: Dec S&P TR future at about FF+20, year-end at FF+100.
geopolitical: FT report that hawkish officials in Washington and Israel are urging Trump to restart strikes on Iran, landing late Friday.
Continued overseas tensions cited by Goldman as one driver of the market stress.
Possible US copper tariff that physical users may have been front-running.
cross_bank_references: Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Barclays all published S&P targets of 8,700 for 2027 within the past two weeks.
Report cites JPMorgan's and Goldman's positioning data in a companion piece.

tension_points.bull_case: Four of four prior VIX spikes saw the S&P higher a week later (+3.3% average), the Panic Index is at 9.8, the Nasdaq is oversold, and valuations are at 10-year lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Two weeks later the S&P averaged -2.8%. CTAs sell in every scenario, dealers are short gamma and the Fed is still hiking with no rescue.
tension_points.what_invalidates: S&P staying below the CTA triggers with continued CTA selling, or a deeper drawdown beyond the 12% from highs seen so far.

tension_points.bull_case: Companies report firm compute pricing and beat-and-raise quarters, and valuations are at 10-year lows.
tension_points.bear_case: Charts of names that have cut (FFIV, INTC) suggest estimate cuts are coming, and investors see no catalyst.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A new catalyst that turns sentiment, which Callahan says nobody can currently name.
